mechanism_inventory: access-control mismatch on updateTssAddress (tssAddress can update itself; self-referential privilege)
missing invariant enforcement on updateTssAddress (no validation new tssAddress_ is valid/trusted)
wrong lifecycle ordering post-renounceTssAddressUpdater (tssAddress==tssAddressUpdater, same key updates both)
access-control asymmetry on pause/unpause (single pauserAddress, no co-approval for unpause)
external-call failure / DoS via pauserAddress grief (lost pauser locks pause/unpause permanently)
missing zero-address-only guard sufficiency (only address(0) rejected, attacker address accepted)
unauthorized state deletion / privilege transition (post-renounce collapses two authorities into one)

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: After renounceTssAddressUpdater(), tssAddressUpdater is set to tssAddress; a single compromised TSS key then satisfies BOTH checks in updateTssAddress. updateTssAddress allows msg.sender==tssAddress to overwrite tssAddress to any attacker address with no second approval — collapsing a two-party rotation ceremony into one party.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Compromised/malicious TSS key (documented adversarial-validator threat model). After renounce (an intended lifecycle step), only the current tssAddress key is needed.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. renounceTssAddressUpdater() sets updater=tssAddress. 2. Compromised TSS calls updateTssAddress(attacker). 3. Check passes (msg.sender==tssAddress and ==updater). 4. tssAddress overwritten. 5. onReceive/onRevert now trust attacker; attacker forges cross-chain receipts.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol and all users whose cross-chain txns route through the connector.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains TSS role, authorizes arbitrary cross-chain value transfers.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Lifecycle-dependent privilege collapse; two-party separation is a documented security property structurally eliminated post-renounce. Affects core authz state tssAddress.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: pause() and unpause() both gated solely by onlyPauser; no co-approval for unpause. A compromised pauser can unpause during an active exploit; a lost pauser permanently bricks pause/unpause.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Compromised pauserAddress key, or griefer who can DoS pauserAddress.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: Path A: operator pauses during exploit; attacker (pauser) immediately unpauses; exploit continues. Path B: pauser lost/bricked; pause/unpause permanently inaccessible — permanent availability DoS.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Users lose emergency pause protection (A) or connector access (B).
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: A: attacker completes exploit. B: no gain, permanent unavailability.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Different state variable (paused) and actor (pauser) than the TSS mechanism. Single-key unpause is a meaningful degradation; permanent DoS path clears Medium independently.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Missing validation that new tssAddress_ is not an arbitrary/contract address
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: only `if (tssAddress_ == address(0)) revert` — no further validation.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether downstream governance / off-chain TSS coordination validates the new address — not in source.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol users if invalid/attacker address accepted.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: access-control mismatch allowing unprivileged callers to updateTssAddress
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: reverts CallerIsNotTssOrUpdater if neither; unprivileged EOAs rejected.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No fully-unprivileged bypass prior to renunciation.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Control of tssAddress enabling authorization of arbitrary cross-chain value transfers; unimpeded exploit if pause bypassed.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Persistent TSS role after rotation — no recovery once overwritten.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Cross-chain funds routed through connector; protocol availability and pause-protection guarantee.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: (1) Two-party tssAddress/tssAddressUpdater separation eliminated post-renounce. (2) Pause provides no single-key-compromise resistance for unpause.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: TSS-address collapse affects all bridge users — not self-funded/dust/admin-only; pause asymmetry affects protocol-wide guarantees.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: two mechanisms affecting different state variables (tssAddress, paused) and actor paths (TSS key, pauser) carried
